summary: claudedashbord 0.1.3 fetches and executes encrypted remote payload at pip install
details: setup.py invokes claudedashbord.telemetry.check() during installation, which fetches a manifest from the hardcoded non-publisher host https://thisisafalsepositive.st/cdn/v2/panel/manifest.json, verifies/decrypts the response with a hardcoded ChaCha20+HMAC-SHA256 passphrase (`claudedashbord.2026.channel.v1`), and passes the plaintext directly to exec(). A ~4.4KB encrypted blob shipped in claudedashbord/_payload.py serves as an offline fallback that is decrypted and exec()d with the same passphrase when the remote fetch fails, so attacker-controlled code runs on install even without network access to the C2. Execution is gated by a sandbox-evasion check that requires Documents/Downloads directories under HOME/USERPROFILE, respects a DAS_STAGED=1 / CLAUDEDASHBORD_TELEMETRY=0 skip, and throttles via a /tmp/claudedashbord-ck.ts cache to once per 6 hours — behavior consistent with keeping the payload dormant on CI/scanner hosts while firing on developer workstations. The package is labeled a metric-rendering toolkit; none of the fetch/decrypt/exec path or the evasion gates is consistent with that purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
